briefing.text: TERT promoter hotspot mutations (C228T at chr5:1,295,228 and C250T at chr5:1,295,250, hg19) are non-coding and sit in a GC-rich region that whole-exome capture covers poorly, so an exome mutation file often lacks them. Before forming any promoter-mutant group, search data_mutations.txt for TERT rows at or near those positions (5'Flank/upstream classifications) and search all clinical column headers for a TERT promoter status field. If no promoter calls exist, samples cannot be labelled promoter wild-type by default, and a test against an empty or all-wild-type grouping is not a test of the hypothesis.
briefing.reason: Whether the hypothesis variable is present at all determines which analysis is valid; teams must establish this before running any statistics.

briefing.text: A coding TERT mutation (e.g. missense in the gene body) is not a TERT promoter mutation. Check Variant_Classification and Start_Position of every TERT row; promoter mutations lie roughly 124 and 146 bp upstream of the ATG (hg19 1,295,228 / 1,295,250). Exclude coding TERT variants from any promoter-status grouping and say so in the reasoning.
briefing.reason: Prevents substituting a different variable for the one the hypothesis names.

briefing.text: In cBioPortal studies, samples with NA in the mutations column of data_gene_panel_matrix.txt were not sequenced for mutations; they must not be counted as wild-type. Tabulate that column and restrict any mutation-vs-expression comparison to samples that are both mutation-profiled and present in the RNA-seq matrix; report n.
briefing.reason: Treating unprofiled samples as wild-type corrupts the comparison groups.

briefing.text: Mutation, expression and clinical tables may use TCGA barcodes with different suffixes and may include recurrent or normal samples. Join on the 15-character sample ID (TCGA-XX-XXXX-01), check Sample Type, keep one primary tumour per patient, and report the joined n.
briefing.reason: Careless joins silently drop or duplicate samples.

briefing.text: A non-significant result, or no test because the mutant group is empty or tiny, is not evidence that there is no correlation. Report group sizes and an effect size with confidence interval, not only a p-value. Distinguish three cases explicitly: the relevant variable is absent from the data; a valid, adequately powered comparison exists and shows an association; or it exists and shows none.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis is a null claim, so the teams must not treat lack of power or a missing variable as support for it.

briefing.text: TERT mRNA in tumours is low, often zero, skewed and bimodal. Inspect its distribution in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt; if a comparison is made, use log2(RSEM+1) with a rank test (Mann-Whitney) or a two-part test (expressed vs not, then level), and report medians rather than t-tests on raw values.
briefing.reason: Affects choice of statistical method if a valid grouping exists.

briefing.text: TERT expression can be raised by routes other than promoter mutation (TERT amplification/rearrangement, promoter hypermethylation), and IDH-mutant/G-CIMP gliomas typically lack TERT promoter mutations and use ATRX/ALT. If a comparison is made, check TERT copy number in data_cna.txt, IDH1 / G-CIMP fields in the clinical sample file and ATRX mutations, and stratify or adjust (e.g. IDH-wildtype only; handle TERT-amplified samples separately).
briefing.reason: Confounders that can create or hide an association; also, ATRX/IDH status must not be used as a stand-in for promoter status.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume promoter-mutation status can only come from the mutation table or a clinical column. Neither tested whether anything else in the study (for example a sample-level annotation) encodes telomere-maintenance or TERT status.

Both teams assume the label 'Not verifiable' fits when the grouping variable is missing, even though the outcome variable (TERT mRNA) is present. This is a judgement about the task's labels, not something either team tested.
unused_evidence: The MAF does contain non-coding calls: 5'UTR, upstream, intron and non_coding_transcript variants. Neither team said how often promoter-region calls appear genome-wide, which would show whether non-coding regions near promoters were captured at all or whether TERT is just a coding-only absence.
The TERT row in the CNA, linear CNA and mRNA tables, and the IDH1/G-CIMP sample columns, were not used. They cannot stand in for promoter status, so ignoring them should not change the label.
The gene panel matrix: 291 samples have mutation profiling (WXS) and the rest are NA. The teams counted these but did not relate them to the samples that have mRNA data.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: promoter status might be stored somewhere it did not search. Team A partly resolved this by searching the clinical headers and the chr5 region, but did not search the matrix files' gene or row identifiers.

Team B: a hidden annotation under another name. Team B only checked for the string 'TERT' in the clinical files. The sample columns (subtype, MGMT, methylation, G-CIMP, IDH1, TMB) show no such field, which in practice resolves it.
second_readings: The hypothesis could be read as a claim of no association that 'True' would support if no promoter-mutant group were found. That reading confuses absence of data with absence of effect. Both teams rejected it, rightly.
'TERT promoter mutations' could be loosened to 'any TERT alteration' (the 1 coding missense call or TERT amplification). That would answer a different hypothesis. Both teams declined to substitute.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed 'Not verifiable' label highly. The MAF is GRCh37 WXS with a single coding TERT missense call and no calls at the promoter hotspots, and no clinical column carries TERT status. The remaining risks are a search gap and the reading of the labels, not a flaw in the analysis.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Count the MAF calls classified as upstream_gene_variant or 5'Flank, or lying within 500 bp upstream of any gene's transcription start, across all genes. Is the near-total absence of such calls consistent with exome capture that excludes the TERT promoter, and does that change how firmly you state that the variable is missing rather than simply wild-type?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Search the row identifiers of the CNA, mRNA, RPPA and z-score matrices, and every distinct value of every sample-clinical column, for TERT, telomere, promoter, C228 or C250. Does any hit change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You searched hotspot positions 1295228/1295250 in GRCh37 coordinates. Confirm that NCBI_Build is GRCh37 for every MAF row and that no call falls within about 2 kb upstream of the TERT TSS under either build. Does any row change your conclusion?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: List every distinct value of each sample-level clinical column (subtype, MGMT, methylation, G-CIMP, IDH1). Does any column encode TERT or telomere-maintenance status indirectly, and if so, does that change your method?

Do standard whole-exome capture kits used in large tumour sequencing consortia around 2008-2013 cover the TERT core promoter (the region about 100-250 bp upstream of the ATG), and is it typically called in their somatic MAFs?
questions.why: This settles whether a missing promoter call means 'not measured' or 'wild-type', which is the core of the Not verifiable label.
